articles.title: India's Tax Dragnet Tightens Around NRIs. The July 1 Overhaul Will Make Hiding Assets Nearly Impossible.
articles.excerpt: A new cross-border information-sharing framework compresses response times to 15 days, assigns dedicated tracking officers, and pulls crypto into the net — all without creating a single new tax.
articles.image_caption: Tax documents and a calculator on a desk — the tools of cross-border compliance
articles.nri_angle: NRIs across the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf face tighter scrutiny on foreign bank accounts, RSUs, property, and crypto holdings as India's tax information exchange system accelerates from July 1.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Scrapped Bond Taxes for Foreign Investors. One Billion Dollars Arrived in Three Days.
articles.excerpt: The abolition of withholding and capital gains taxes on government securities has triggered a buying spree, compressed yields, and revived India's bid for Bloomberg index inclusion — all while the rupee fights a losing battle against oil prices.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai's Fort district
articles.nri_angle: NRIs choosing between FCNR deposits and government bonds now face a genuinely competitive choice — zero-tax bonds at 6.9% versus 7.1% deposit rates with RBI-backed swap incentives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thirty-Two Words in Ninety Seconds: Shrey Parikh Wins the 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee
articles.excerpt: The fourteen-year-old from Rancho Cucamonga shattered the spell-off record and extended Indian Americans' two-decade dominance of the country's premier academic competition.
articles.image_caption: A contestant at the Scripps National Spelling Bee competition in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American community has dominated the Spelling Bee for two decades; the victory reflects the diaspora's deep investment in academic competition and a self-reinforcing ecosystem of coaching, regional circuits, and family aspiration.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Diaspora Dollars Hit $135 Billion — and They Are the Only Foreign Capital That Never Flinches
articles.excerpt: Record remittances in FY25 financed nearly half of India's trade deficit. With $140 billion projected for FY26, the NRI wire transfer has quietly become India's most reliable external lifeline.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: NRI remittances are the largest single source of hard currency flowing into India, outpacing FDI and FPI; the shift from Gulf blue-collar to US/UK white-collar sources reflects the diaspora's upward mobility; individual NRIs benefit from a weak rupee and competitive deposit rates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Forty Thousand Restaurants and No Chain: India's Celebrity Chefs Are Finally Coming for the American Market
articles.excerpt: Sanjeev Kapoor in Santa Clara, Zorawar Kalra in Bellevue, Rishtedar in Miami — three branded Indian restaurant concepts have opened their first US outposts, betting that the country's $15 billion Indian food market is ready for its Chipotle moment.
articles.image_caption: An array of Indian dishes — the US Indian restaurant market is now valued at $15 billion
articles.nri_angle: The Indian restaurant market in the US has been built entirely by diaspora independents; the arrival of branded chains from India connects NRI diners to cultural touchstones from home while raising questions about mainstreaming vs. authenticity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Dead, Three Ships Hit: Indian Sailors Are Caught in the Crossfire of America's Iran Blockade
articles.excerpt: In the deadliest week for Indian merchant seafarers in years, U.S. Navy strikes on three tankers off Oman killed three crew and forced scores to abandon ship — prompting India to summon the American diplomat twice and demand the attacks stop.
articles.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea — Indian-crewed vessels have been repeatedly struck by U.S. forces off the coast of Oman
articles.nri_angle: India has 300,000+ seafarers working globally, many from working-class families who depend on maritime income. The Gulf crisis threatens both lives and livelihoods across the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Silicon Valley's Indian Americans Take Their Case to the FBI as Hindu Temple Attacks Spread Across the Bay Area
articles.excerpt: A group of prominent Indian Americans held an extraordinary meeting with federal officials and four police departments this week, demanding faster action on a wave of anti-Hindu vandalism and theft targeting Bay Area temples.
articles.image_caption: A Hindu temple in Sunnyvale, California — Bay Area temples have faced a wave of vandalism and hate-motivated attacks
articles.nri_angle: The Bay Area's Indian-American community — among the wealthiest and most professionally accomplished in the country — confronts the unsettling reality that its sacred spaces are being targeted, forcing community leaders into unfamiliar territory as security advocates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Macron Open Bharat Innovates in Nice. The Real Story Is the 120 Startups Behind Them.
articles.excerpt: India's maiden deep-tech showcase brings 120 startups, 500 investors, and 13 sectors to the French Riviera — one day before the G7.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with French President Emmanuel Macron at a bilateral meeting in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: The conclave gives NRI investors and entrepreneurs in Europe a structured way to connect with Indian innovation, while showcasing India's deep-tech ecosystem to global capital for the first time at this scale.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Margin of Seventy People: India Just Overtook England as Australia's Largest Source of Overseas-Born Residents
articles.excerpt: For the first time since records began in 1891, a non-British-origin group tops Australia's migration charts. The Indian-born population grew by 522,000 in a decade.
articles.image_caption: The Sydney Opera House and harbour — home to one of Australia's largest Indian-born communities
articles.nri_angle: Nearly a million Indians now call Australia home, making it the fourth-largest Indian diaspora community in the world. The milestone reshapes the conversation about belonging and identity for Indian Australians.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: King Charles Marks the British Asian Trust's 20th Year With a £1 Million Gala. The Timing Is Not Coincidental.
articles.excerpt: The monarch's charity has supported 18.8 million people across South Asia. At a London gala held against the backdrop of anti-Asian unrest, his presence sent a pointed message about community and belonging.
articles.image_caption: King Charles III, Royal Founding Patron of the British Asian Trust
articles.nri_angle: The King's charity, built around British Asian identity, has supported 18.8 million people in South Asia — and his visible patronage during anti-Asian unrest sends a signal to the 1.9 million Indians in the UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Opened Its Stock Markets to Every Foreigner on the Planet. NRIs Are No Longer Special.
articles.excerpt: A quiet FEMA amendment published on June 12 replaces the phrase 'NRI or OCI' with 'any individual residing outside India,' dismantling a decades-old investment privilege the diaspora once had to itself.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai's Dalal Street financial district
articles.nri_angle: NRIs and OCIs who long enjoyed exclusive retail access to Indian equities now share that privilege with every foreign individual — a levelling that could reshape how diaspora investors think about their edge in India's capital markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From the Lincoln Memorial to Times Square: How Yoga Day 2026 Became the Diaspora's Biggest Public Ritual
articles.excerpt: The Indian Embassy will host its flagship Yoga Day celebration at the Lincoln Memorial on June 19, while Padma Shri HR Nagendra — Modi's personal yoga guru — headlines the Times Square event on June 21.
articles.image_caption: A group practising yoga outdoors in a park setting
articles.nri_angle: International Day of Yoga has evolved from a UN calendar date into the Indian diaspora's most visible annual public gathering in the West — a rare moment when thousands of Indian Americans occupy iconic American landmarks to practise something unmistakably Indian.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Dame Parveen Kumar Gets the GBE. She Is Now One of Britain's Most Decorated Indian-Born Citizens.
articles.excerpt: The 2026 King's Birthday Honours list, published on June 12, names at least eight British Indians — but the headline belongs to a gastroenterologist from Lahore who spent 40 years in the NHS.
articles.image_caption: Dame Parveen Kumar, elevated to GBE in the 2026 Birthday Honours
articles.nri_angle: The Birthday Honours remain the most visible annual scoreboard for British Indian professional achievement — and the 2026 list, with a GBE at the top, signals that the community's influence now reaches the highest tiers of the British establishment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: GIFT City Is No Longer a Policy Experiment. NRI Wealth Managers Are Starting to Notice.
articles.excerpt: India's first international financial services centre has approved its inaugural family investment fund, drawn endorsements from Singapore's diplomats, and begun attracting Gulf-based NRI capital fleeing regional instability.
articles.image_caption: Brihaspati via wikimedia (BY-SA)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs managing wealth across multiple jurisdictions now have a credible India-linked alternative to Dubai and Singapore — one that offers tax advantages, lower costs, and direct access to Indian markets without the regulatory friction of onshore investing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Few Dollars in His Pocket, Thirty-Five Years Later: Arvind Raman Now Runs America's Standards Agency
articles.excerpt: The Indian-born engineer who arrived at Purdue with almost nothing has been confirmed by the U.S. Senate as director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology — and undersecretary of commerce.
articles.image_caption: Neil Armstrong Hall of Engineering at Purdue University, where Arvind Raman served as dean
articles.nri_angle: Raman's journey from India to the helm of NIST — the agency that sets America's technology standards — is a distilled version of the Indian immigrant arc: arrive with nothing, build a career through sheer competence, and end up shaping the infrastructure of the country that took you in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Karnataka's New Chief Minister Has a Plan for 1.8 Million Overseas Kannadigas: Give Them Their Own Department
articles.excerpt: Ten days into his tenure, D.K. Shivakumar is reviving a Congress manifesto promise to create a dedicated NRI department — modelled on Kerala's — to channel diaspora investment and address the grievances of Kannadigas abroad.
articles.image_caption: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar addressing a public gathering
articles.nri_angle: For the estimated 1.8 million Kannadigas scattered across 34 countries, the promise of a dedicated state department means a single window for investment facilitation, property disputes, and welfare support — replacing the current maze of uncoordinated bureaucratic departments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nice, Bratislava, Evian, Paris: Modi's Six-Day European Tour Begins and Ends With the Diaspora
articles.excerpt: The prime minister's France-Slovakia swing combines G7 diplomacy with startup diplomacy and a community address in Paris — the first by an Indian leader at VivaTech.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who departed for France on June 13 for a six-day European tour
articles.nri_angle: Modi will address the Indian community in Paris on June 18 and inaugurate Bharat Innovates in Nice — both directly aimed at diaspora entrepreneurs and professionals in Europe. The visit also raises H-1B visa and trade deal questions that affect every NRI in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's OCI Cards Have Gone Digital. Here Is What Five Million Holders Need to Know.
articles.excerpt: The Citizenship Amendment Rules 2026, notified on April 30, introduce e-OCI registration, mandatory online applications, biometric consent for fast-track immigration, and a ban on dual passports for minors.
articles.image_caption: A traveller checks their smartphone at an airport — the kind of scene where the new e-OCI could replace a physical card
articles.nri_angle: Every OCI card holder — over 5 million people, mostly in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia — is directly affected. Paper applications are dead. The e-OCI could eliminate the dreaded renewal queue. But mandatory biometric consent and the minor dual-passport ban raise new compliance questions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tomorrow, Dartmouth Hands Vivek Murthy an Honorary Doctorate. He Will Probably Talk About Loneliness Again.
articles.excerpt: The first Indian-American U.S. Surgeon General, who served under both Obama and Biden, receives an honorary Doctor of Science as the Class of 2026 graduates in Hanover, New Hampshire.
articles.image_caption: Dr. Vivek Murthy during his tenure as U.S. Surgeon General
articles.nri_angle: Murthy is arguably the most prominent Indian American in US public health history. His parents immigrated from Karnataka, he was raised in Miami, and he has repeatedly credited the Indian concept of Seva — selfless service — as the force behind his work. His loneliness research, his social media youth warnings, and his Parting Prescription for America all grew from a worldview shaped between two cultures.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Twenty-One Years, One Gopuram: Berlin's Sri Ganesha Temple Opens as One of Europe's Largest Hindu Shrines
articles.excerpt: Black granite carved in Tamil Nadu, water from the Ganges poured by crane, and a Modi-Merz visit pencilled for October — the Neukölln temple is the diaspora's most ambitious European construction project in a generation.
articles.image_caption: The Sri Ganesha Hindu Temple in Berlin's Neukölln district on the day of its consecration, June 7, 2026
articles.nri_angle: A two-decade community effort by Berlin's Tamil Hindu diaspora — students, IT workers, Sri Lankan refugees — built one of Europe's largest Hindu temples entirely through donations and volunteer labour, creating a permanent spiritual anchor for South Asians across Germany.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Banks Are Racing to Offer NRIs Up to 7.1% on Dollar Deposits. The RBI Engineered the Whole Thing.
articles.excerpt: A central bank intervention designed to shore up the rupee has turned FCNR deposits into the hottest NRI financial product in a decade, with leverage potentially pushing returns past 20 per cent.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee notes and coins — NRI deposits are now at the centre of a central bank strategy to attract dollars
articles.nri_angle: NRIs holding dollars in US or Gulf bank accounts now face a rare window — three-to-five-year FCNR deposits in Indian banks offering returns that rival equities, tax-free in India, with principal fully repatriable. The catch: the scheme closes September 30.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fifty Years of Chariots on Fifth Avenue: New York's Ratha Yatra Marks a Half-Century of Krishna in America
articles.excerpt: What began as a handful of Hare Krishna devotees pulling a homemade chariot through Manhattan in 1976 has become one of the city's longest-running religious processions — and a barometer of how deeply Indian spiritual traditions have rooted in American soil.
articles.image_caption: Devotees pull a Ratha Yatra chariot through a street in the United States
articles.nri_angle: The NYC Ratha Yatra's 50th anniversary reflects a half-century arc of Indian spiritual culture embedding in America — from counterculture curiosity to mainstream cultural institution, with the festival now drawing as many first-generation Indian professionals and families as it does Western-born devotees.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Indian Missions, One Week, Same Warning: Stop Picking Up the Phone
articles.excerpt: Consulates in Toronto, New York, and the Bay Area are all sounding the alarm on a coordinated wave of phone scams targeting NRIs — and the timing tells you why.
articles.image_caption: A smartphone displaying a fraud alert notification
articles.nri_angle: NRIs across North America are being targeted by sophisticated phone scams impersonating Indian consular officials, exploiting immigration anxieties in the current political climate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fifteen Languages, Three Days, One Theatre: NYIFF 2026 Is the Most Important Indian Film Festival You Have Never Heard Of
articles.excerpt: The New York Indian Film Festival returns for its 26th edition next week with Nawazuddin Siddiqui, a Dil Chahta Hai anniversary screening, and films in languages spoken by fewer than two million people.
articles.image_caption: Nawazuddin Siddiqui at an Indian film festival
articles.nri_angle: NYIFF is a cultural lifeline for Indian Americans seeking cinema that reflects the diversity of their homeland — far beyond the Bollywood mainstream — and a launchpad for filmmakers from India's margins.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Hyderabad's JNTU to Alabama's Rocket City: Srinath Ekkad Named Engineering Dean at UAH
articles.excerpt: A thermal sciences researcher who started at Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University will now lead one of America's most aerospace-connected engineering colleges.
articles.image_caption: The Engineering Building at the University of Alabama in Huntsville
articles.nri_angle: Ekkad's appointment extends a pattern of Indian-origin academics reaching the highest rungs of American university leadership, from JNTU undergrad to dean of UAH's 3,000-student engineering college.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Sports Ministry Has Sent a 'Sports Passport' Proposal to the PM's Office. For Diaspora Athletes, It Changes Everything.
articles.excerpt: If approved, the framework could let PIO and OCI athletes represent India in international competition without surrendering foreign citizenship — a first in Indian sports history, and a potential game-changer ahead of the 2036 Olympics bid.
articles.image_caption: India's national football team in action during the 2018 SAFF Championship
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indian-origin athletes who grew up playing football, tennis, and basketball in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia have been legally barred from representing India. The Sports Passport proposal directly addresses the diaspora's exclusion from Indian national teams.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Decades at MIT Press, and Now She Runs Columbia's. Meet Gita Manaktala.
articles.excerpt: Columbia University has appointed the Indian American publishing leader as Executive Director of one of the nation's oldest and most respected university presses — a quiet milestone in a field where South Asian representation at the top remains rare.
articles.image_caption: Columbia University's Morningside Heights campus in New York City
articles.nri_angle: Manaktala's appointment adds to the growing but still thin ranks of Indian Americans leading major American academic and cultural institutions — a quieter form of diaspora achievement than tech CEO headlines, but one that shapes what knowledge gets published, who gets heard, and which ideas reach global audiences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Fifty-Six Years After a Prayer at Le Bourget, France Is Getting Its First Traditional Hindu Temple
articles.excerpt: The BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Bussy-Saint-Georges opens in September with a thirteen-day Festival of Culture — a milestone for Europe's Indian diaspora that began with a 1970 airport layover.
articles.image_caption: Carved stone deities at a traditional Hindu temple — the same craft tradition behind the Paris mandir
articles.nri_angle: The Paris mandir fills a gap for hundreds of thousands of Indians across Western Europe who have lacked a traditionally built stone temple, and its September inauguration is already drawing NRI families from the US, UK, and Gulf into pilgrimage-tourism packages.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Singapore Just Blocked Fourteen Posts Targeting Its Indian Community. The Content Likely Came from China.
articles.excerpt: The city-state invoked its Online Criminal Harms Act to order YouTube, Facebook, and X to disable videos claiming Singapore was being 'overrun by Indians' — a rare, swift use of state power to defend diaspora communities.
articles.image_caption: A street in Little India, Singapore, adorned with colourful cultural decorations
articles.nri_angle: Singapore's decisive legal intervention to protect its Indian minority offers a sharp contrast to how other countries with large NRI populations have responded to anti-Indian sentiment — and raises questions about what legal tools are available elsewhere.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seven 'Ratnas' and a 57-Year Legacy: Inside the AIA-NY Annual Benefit Gala 2026
articles.excerpt: The oldest Indian-American organisation honoured a xenotransplantation pioneer, a Harvard AI entrepreneur, and five other trailblazers at a packed Flushing gathering — then announced plans for its 39th Deepavali celebration.
articles.image_caption: The Association of Indians in America held its annual gala at Terrace on the Park in Flushing, New York
articles.nri_angle: Oldest Indian-American organisation (founded 1967) honours new generation of NRI achievers; event bridges generational and professional divides in the community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Coming Home to Concrete: How the Gulf War Is Fuelling a Kerala Property Rush Among NRIs
articles.excerpt: Four months of conflict in West Asia have pushed Gulf-based Keralites to hedge their futures with flats and plots back home — even as construction costs surge 35 per cent and builders struggle to keep up.
articles.image_caption: New residential developments in Kochi, Kerala, where NRI property demand has surged amid the West Asia conflict
articles.nri_angle: Gulf-based Keralite NRIs — one of India's largest remittance communities — are reassessing permanent settlement plans; war is accelerating a generational shift from 'earn abroad, retire home' to 'invest now, return sooner.'
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
